title: EchoXFlow: A Beamspace Echocardiography Dataset for Cardiac Motion, Flow, and Function
claim: Raw native-geometry modality streams hold more information than the filtered, scan-converted clinical view derived from them.
layout: 3 groups, left-to-right, raw streams then arrow then clinical view
description: The figure runs left to right. On the left are three stacked, separate raw data panels in native beamspace geometry. Brightness Mode is a tall grayscale ultrasound strip. Doppler Velocity is a blocky, noisy blue/red/yellow map. Doppler Power is a dark yellow-green map. Each panel has a white overlay label giving its tensor dimensions (T, H, W). A long black arrow in the middle is labeled 'Physical Units, Cartesian Conversion' above it and 'Nonlinear filtering, Smoothing' below it. On the right is the 'Clinical View', a fan-shaped sector ultrasound image. It has a smooth blue and red Doppler overlay inside a white-outlined box, green depth ticks at 5 and 10, and a velocity colorbar from -0.6 to 0.6 m/s. The eye goes first to the colorful Doppler panels and the sector image.
caption: A frame of a color Doppler video in EchoXFlow, which can be scan-converted to a clinical view using metadata such as sector angles and depths. In clinical visualization, Doppler velocities are often smoothed and gated by combining the amplitude of the Doppler signal and the corresponding B-mode frame. Pre-scan-converted data are more efficient to store and process, and contain more information. Here, the Doppler and B-mode frames occur in a temporal 2:1 ratio.
abstract: We introduce EchoXFlow, a clinical echocardiography dataset with ultrasound in its native acquisition geometry. Existing public datasets offer limited opportunities to study how cardiac anatomy, myocardial motion, and blood flow relate: Doppler velocities are typically absent or fused as RGB overlays on grayscale anatomical images, and acquisitions are released only after scan conversion and lossy vendor display processing. EchoXFlow comprises 35,377 recordings from 666 routine-care examinations of 622 patients. It preserves the timing, geometry, and modality relationships needed for physically grounded echo learning. Each recording is retained as separable modality-specific streams: temporally resolved 1D, 2D, and 3D data alongside multiple Doppler modalities, paired with a synchronized ECG. Clinical annotations range from guideline-defined measurements to dense 2D myocardial contours and 3D left-ventricular endocardial meshes. With its associated open-source tooling, EchoXFlow enables cross-modal, acquisition-aware learning tasks that cannot be formulated from conventional scan-converted videos alone, and serves as a testbed for 4D vision and physically grounded multi-modal learning more broadly. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ahus-AIM/EchoXFlow and the tooling at https://github.com/Ahus-AIM/EchoXFlow
